progress_update.summary: Deep design session building on the live-state-poc SSE infrastructure. We refined the RFC's graph communication model — separated edges (structural) from channels (communication), established a 2x2 taxonomy of graph node types (LiveState/Broadcast/LiveAggregation/Stream), explored ownership-based spawn with cascading lifecycle, reactive edges, and scatter-gather patterns. Key late-session insight: workflow state is inherently observable (progress during execution, result on success, frozen on failure), distinct from LiveState which is an explicit standalone coordination node. Critiqued our own work — identified ctx.emit() and invocation introspection as highest-value next steps, parked reactive aggregation and supervision policies as over-designed.
progress_update.goal: Design the next evolution of Restate's process model — from isolated virtual objects to a connected graph of durable processes with structural relationships, efficient communication primitives, and real-time observability. Core principle: observable state is first-class in the model.
accomplished: Squashed 42 commits into 1, validated (cargo fmt/clippy/nextest pass), pushed to `live-state-poc` branch
Wrote RFC: Process Composition Primitives — unified edge model, then refined through multiple critique rounds
Separated edges (structural: relationships, ownership, traversal) from channels (communication: message delivery, fan-out) as distinct primitives
Established 2x2 taxonomy: LiveState (coalescable 1-to-N), Broadcast (ordered 1-to-N), LiveAggregation (coalescable N-to-1), Stream (ordered N-to-1)
Distinguished workflow state (implicit, runtime-managed) from LiveState (explicit, developer-created) — both observable via ego graph SSE
Self-critiqued: identified over-design (reactive aggregation, capability handles, supervision policies) and grounded priorities
progress_update.now: Completed design critique. Identified that the session's most useful output is a principle (observable state is first-class) plus concrete next steps (ctx.emit, introspection, onUpgrade). The RFC needs updating with edges-vs-channels distinction but shipping the SSE POC should not be blocked by it.

Implement ctx.emit() + invocation introspection endpoint (high value, bounded scope)

Write focused design doc on edge storage model (intra-partition first)
Update RFC with edges-vs-channels distinction and four-node taxonomy as conceptual framework
constraints: Cross-partition edges are the hardest unsolved implementation problem — start intra-partition
Broadcast channels need partition-local subscriber lists backed by Bifrost, not edge traversal
OTP analogies useful for vocabulary but Restate's durability changes failure semantics fundamentally
Don't let the RFC/vision work block shipping the working SSE POC
decisions: Edges model structure, channels model communication — two distinct primitives
Four graph node types: LiveState, Broadcast, LiveAggregation, Stream — distinguished by compaction policy and data flow direction
Workflow state is implicit and runtime-managed (progress during execution, result on success, frozen on failure). LiveState is explicit and developer-managed. Both observable.
Observable state is first-class in the model — the core design principle
ctx.emit() and invocation introspection are highest-value lowest-complexity features to ship next
Parked: reactive aggregation, capability handles, supervision policies, selective receive — revisit when real demand emerges
open_questions: How does broadcast channel partition-local subscriber list interact with repartitioning?
How does the runtime set workflow result into state on completion — new key? merge?
What's the minimum SDK surface to validate the edge model?

risks: Vision is compelling but far from implementation — risk of over-designing before proving foundations
Cross-partition edge consistency may require weaker guarantees than expected
The four-node taxonomy may collapse further once implementation reveals constraints
Session generated features from OTP analogy rather than user stories — need real use cases to validate

continuity.arc_goal: Sessions 1-3 built SSE infrastructure (StateRouter, repartition support, state change detection). Session 4 pivoted to larger vision (RFC, edge model, OTP comparison). Session 5 critiqued and refined — separated edges from channels, established taxonomy, grounded priorities. The arc moves from working infrastructure to design vision to pragmatic next steps.
